questions.learningObjective: Apply nuclear family to a study of family structure.

stimulus.body: A 2005 census study of 450 retirees in West Africa found 58% lived in nuclear households, while 30% lived in extended or other arrangements.

questions.stem: Explain the 2005 Africa finding about family structure.

answer.exemplar: A 2005 census study of 450 retirees in West Africa found 58% lived in nuclear households, while 30% lived in extended or other arrangements. This illustrates nuclear family: a household of parents and their children. A careful reading links the group-level pattern to the wider social structure rather than to any single person, and it distinguishes this idea from competing accounts that locate the cause elsewhere.

questions.explanation: The finding illustrates nuclear family: a household of parents and their children. The 58 percent versus 30 percent split in West Africa shows why this reading fits better than the alternatives.
questions.hint: Think about the social force behind the two figures.
